purpose: Progressive-disclosure manifest for one governed Freedom 250 research package.
title: Banks and Credit Unions — Federal and Four-State Legal Architecture
question: What legally distinguishes banks from credit unions, which rules come from the federal government, and how do Florida, Wyoming, New York and Texas use their remaining charter, public-deposit, tax, supervision and digital-asset authority?
bluf: The United States has overlapping bank and credit-union dual-charter systems rather than one national regime. Charter, ownership, regulator, insurer, account eligibility, public-funds permission, digital authority and operating state must be recorded separately. Florida and Texas maintain active state-bank and state-credit-union charters and admit credit unions to public deposits; New York maintains both charters but its ordinary local-deposit law still excludes credit unions; Wyoming charters banks and SPDIs but has no current state-credit-union law, so its credit unions are federally chartered even when state law admits them to public funds.
entities: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
New York Department of Financial Services
